description:
FILED s435 (Opus 5) FROM A LIVE EVENT, not a suspicion: on 2026-08-23 at
00:11:27 a single compiler-side perl reached 7.76 GB anon RSS / 9.7 GB VM,
exhausted the 4 GB swap (Free swap = 200 kB) and made the machine
unresponsive until the kernel's GLOBAL oom-killer took it
(dmesg: task=perl, pid=422916, total-vm:9712848kB, anon-rss:7759348kB,
task_memcg=/user.slice/.../ptyxis-spawn-...scope).  The session hung with it.

THE CAUSE was a compiler bug, and an ordinary one: an in-flight edit left
Pl::Parser::_drop_site calling ITSELF (a helper stub whose body had not yet
been filled in with the extracted site computation).  Perl has no tail-call
elimination, so every frame allocated; the process climbed until the box
died.  Fixed in the same session -- but the bug is not the point:

THE POINT IS THAT THE COMPILER SIDE HAS NO CAP.  Any runaway in Pl/** --
infinite recursion, an unterminated parse loop, a string appended to in a
loop -- costs the whole MACHINE, not the run.  Measured both ways:

  unbounded:              7.7 GB, swap gone, machine hung, ~minutes, global OOM
  ( ulimit -v 4000000 ):  dies in ~5 s with
                          "Deep recursion on subroutine Pl::Parser::_drop_site
                           at Pl/Parser.pm line 9313"
                          "Out of memory in perl:util:safesysmalloc"
                          -- i.e. the cap TURNS THE HANG INTO A DIAGNOSIS that
                          names the sub and the line.

Note the deep-recursion warning DID fire unbounded too (depth 100), scrolled
past, and changed nothing: a warning does not stop the allocation.  The cap is
what makes the failure survivable, and it also covers the runaways NO warning
exists for (a growing string, an unterminated loop).

WHAT EXISTS ALREADY -- the pattern is in the tree, on ONE runner only:
tools/run-perl-suite.pl:163-166 wraps its run in
`systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=10G -p MemorySwapMax=1G` (probed for
availability first), and its per-file children get `ulimit -v 4194304`
(lines 569-587).  That is why op/list.t's 10 GB OOM (#160) is a QUARANTINED
row and not a dead machine.  Nothing else has a cap: not pl2cl / runpcl, not
sweep-perl-tests.pl, not Pl/t/PCLCore.pm (the gate), not tools/corpus-diff.pl,
tools/drop-census.pl, tools/gate-set-scan.pl, tools/emission-ab.pl.

SHAPE TO DECIDE (this is the ask -- do not just widen ulimit everywhere):
The five SBCL runners already share ONE command-line builder
(tools/lib/PCLSbcl.pm, CLAUDE.md "THE FIVE RUNNERS"); the PERL side has no
equivalent seam, and that is the actual gap.  Candidates:
  (a) one shared helper (tools/lib/PCLLimits.pm?) that every compiler-side
      entry point calls, capping address space at a configurable default
      (env override, e.g. PCL_MEM_CAP_MB / PCL_NO_MEM_CAP=1 for a deliberate
      big run).  Perl cannot lower its own RLIMIT_AS without BSD::Resource
      (not core), so the cap is either a re-exec under `sh -c 'ulimit -v N;
      exec ...'` or the systemd-run scope run-perl-suite.pl already uses --
      the scope also catches the SBCL side and any orphan.
  (b) scope-only: wrap the RUNNERS (sweep, gate, the census tools), leave a
      bare ./pl2cl uncapped.  Cheaper, but the event above was a bare tool
      run, which is exactly the case it would miss.
  (c) do nothing in code; document the ulimit in the runbook.  Rejected here
      on the measurement: an operator who has to remember it is the operator
      who loses a machine (the same argument that made the sweep's TIMEOUT
      retry automatic, #176).
Cost of a cap when nothing is wrong: zero -- it only fires on a runaway.
Choose the number from a measurement, not a guess: record the peak RSS of the
heaviest legitimate compile (pack.t's transpile, the uni/ corpus) first, so
the cap sits above it with headroom.

ACCEPTANCE: a deliberately runaway compile (a two-line self-recursive helper
in a scratch copy) run through each capped entry point dies within seconds
with perl's own out-of-memory message, and `free -m` shows swap untouched;
plus a guard row asserting the cap is applied (and that PCL_NO_MEM_CAP=1
removes it).  The gate's wall time must not move.


=== DONE s436 (Opus 5), commit 3d289f8.  Ruled option (a) at the pl2cl seam.
A BEGIN block before PPI loads re-execs the ORIGINAL argv (read from
/proc/self/cmdline, so perl's own -I survives) through
`sh -c 'ulimit -v N; exec "$@"'`.  PCL_MEM_CAP_MB / PCL_NO_MEM_CAP /
PCL_SHOW_MEM_CAP.  Default 4096 MB, measured against the heaviest legitimate
transpiles (~140 MB peak address space).  Acceptance run for real: a scratch
tree with a self-recursive helper dies in 3.9 s naming the sub and the line,
swap untouched.  Cost unmeasurable (20 transpiles: 2.276 s vs 2.287 s).
--bundle/--executable exempt (SBCL reserves address space).  Guard
Pl/t/mem-cap-01.t.

STILL OPEN â the RESIDUE, which is why this task is worth re-reading: the ~40
Pl/t files that `use Pl::Parser` IN PROCESS never spawn pl2cl and are
therefore still uncapped, so an in-flight edit can hang the machine from the
GATE exactly as it did from a bare tool run.  The obvious complement is the
pattern already in tools/run-perl-suite.pl: wrap tools/prove-core in
`systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=â¦` (RSS-based, so SBCL's
address-space reservation is irrelevant; ~30 ms once; covers every process the
gate starts).  NOT done â the ruling named the pl2cl seam and widening a ruled
shape unilaterally is not this session's call.  Ask 1 of
docs/opus5-review-requests-s436.md.
subject: The COMPILER SIDE has no memory cap: a runaway in Pl/** costs the MACHINE, not the run (measured s435 -- 7.7 GB perl, swap exhausted, global OOM); run-perl-suite.pl's systemd scope + ulimit is the only guard in the tree
